After 10 greeting bytes have been read, the low bit of byte 9 is zero for the staged witness, so this check marks the peer unversioned. That dispatch selects the ZMTP/1.0 handshake path that later instantiates the vulnerable static allocator.

The unversioned handshake constructs `v1_decoder_t` on `c_single_allocator`. `_options.in_batch_size` defaults to 8192, and the saved ASan allocation stack shows `c_single_allocator::c_single_allocator` mallocs a single 8192-byte `_buf` for this decoder.

Because `one_byte_size_ready()` saw the leading size byte `0xff`, this function parses the next eight witness bytes `00 00 00 00 00 00 c8 00` as `payload_length = 51200`. The zero-length, max-message-size, and `size_t`-range guards in this function do not reject that value.
Subtracting the flags byte converts the accepted long-frame payload length into `msg_size = 51199`, the body length that exceeds the fixed allocator size of 8192.
After `init_size (msg_size)` succeeds and the witness flags byte `0x00` is stored, `flags_ready()` points `_read_pos` at the message body storage and sets `_to_read = _in_progress.size() = 51199`.

With `_to_read = 51199` and the static allocator still reporting 8192, `get_buffer()` takes the large-message zero-copy branch and asks the caller to read directly into `_read_pos` instead of the allocator buffer `_buf`.

On one earlier zero-copy body read, `read (_inpos, bufsize)` returns 8215 bytes, so this assignment stores `_insize = 8215`. The later crashing `size_ = 8215` shows such a read occurred, because this read-count state is what the engine propagates into the allocator.
Immediately after that body read, the stream engine forwards the 8215-byte `_insize` value into the decoder allocator state.

Root cause. The fixed allocator copies `new_size_` into `_buf_size`, so the prior 8215-byte body read changes the logical allocator size to 8215 even though the backing `_buf` is still the original 8192-byte heap allocation from step 2.

Because the body read used the zero-copy destination from step 6 (`data_ == _read_pos`), `decode()` consumes that same 8215-byte chunk without copying, advances `_read_pos`, and reduces `_to_read` by 8215. Repeated executions of this zero-copy update on the same message eventually leave the remaining tail smaller than the stale allocator size 8215.

When a later call sees `_to_read < _allocator.size ()`, `get_buffer()` falls through to the static allocator buffer. `_buf` is still the original 8192-byte allocation from step 2, but `_allocator.size()` now reports 8215 because of step 9, so this branch returns an oversized `(data, size)` pair for the next socket read.
